author: Kwan-Chen Ma
title: Nvidia: Out China - NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)
text:
Citing a slow China demand, Apple's ( AAPL ) Q1 downside guidance serves as a wake-up call to the entire stock market. Most cyclical tech stocks especially Nvidia ( NVDA ) reacted harshly to the announcement (-6.1%), as the warning ignited a widespread worry of a trade war-induced global recession. In a way, Nvidia's sharp reaction may suggest the possibility that China's slowdown can quickly proliferate through the global demand chain, considering that Nvidia generated more than 50% its revenue from Greater China region. In this post, I looked into this possibility.
Nvidia's China Relevance First, we want to examine how important China is to Nvidia. Historically, Nvidia's revenue comes from five geographical segments: Taiwan (29%), China (22%), U.S. (13%), Europe (7%), and the rest of the world (29%) (Figure 1 and Figure 1B). China has not been a major player until 2016 when its revenue contribution started picking up Taiwan's share (Figure 1C). By fiscal Q3, 2019, China's revenue reached near $800 million and 22% of Nvidia's total revenue (Figure 1 and Figure 2).
The Bad News Furthermore, if adding the rest of Asia to the Greater China segment, including the largest revenue Taiwan segment, the "Asia influence" cannot be underestimated because it would account for close to 70% of Nvidia's revenue. However, other than its growing size, China's presence becomes even more relevant as the economies in the rest of the world become increasingly more correlated with China's economy. Therefore, China's recession will not be confined to China. In fact, for Nvidia's U.S. shareholders' perspective, Asia's impact on company's revenue is much more important than the U.S. or Europe's impact, as Nvidia total revenue is more affected by Asia's revenue growth than by the U.S. (Figure 4A).
The real bad news is that, if China's slowdown may be to blame for part of Nvidia's recent downward slide, the damage to Nvidia's shareholders will not be the end of it. Considering that Nvidia's China revenue growth has been increasingly correlated with Nvidia's U.S. revenue growth (Figure 4B), China's slowdown in demand either from crypto, gaming, or trade war weakness may soon be transmitted to the U.S. As a result, the negative impact on Nvidia's total revenue will be further compounded, considering that Nvidia has another 30% of revenue from U.S. and Europe (Figure 1B).
The Good News The silver lining of the high correlation on the downside is that Taiwan and Europe are the two Nvidia revenue sources which counteract China and U.S. revenue growth in a meaningful way, as Taiwan and Europe contribute more than 36% of Nvidia total revenue (Figure 1C and Figure 4B).
Revenue Impact on Nvidia Stock Price To Nvidia shareholders, maybe the more important question is how the correlated revenue growths affect Nvidia stock prices. Using the above relationship, we were able to estimate the correlated impact on all five Nvidia segments in terms of their segment revenue growths and Nvidia share prices, assuming 1% drop in China revenue growth rate (Table 1). The way to read Table 1 is like this: For every 1% decrease in China revenue growth rate, U.S. segment will also lose -0.45%, and Taiwan and Europe will gain 0.15% and 0.11% instead. In short, 1% China revenue loss will result in Nvidia's total revenue loss of about 1.51%. The corresponding stock price impact is that Nvidia stock price will drop $2.75 and $0.91 from the China and U.S. loss in revenue but gain $0.34 from Taiwan's 0.15% gain in revenue. The bottom line is that the net impact on Nvidia's share price, considering the correlated revenue growth between five segments is a loss of $3.78 for every 1% drop in China growth rate.
When Tim Cook lowered the Q1 revenue guidance from the original $89-94 billion range to $84 billion, or approximately a 6% reduction, he cited the miss was mainly due to China's revenue loss. As Nvidia has over 50% revenue exposure from Greater China region, while Apple has about $25% China revenue exposure, it may be likely that Nvidia may risk a 10% reduction in revenue in the coming quarters. Given that China has a 1.51 total revenue multiple, a 10% total revenue loss is equivalent to about 6.6% China revenue loss. Using an optimistic assumption that the resulting next quarter miss is contained within the same quarter, Nvidia share price should have dropped by - $25 the day of the Apple's downside.
Incidentally, Nvidia stock price lost -$9 on January 2, amid Cook's announcement, but the loss quickly reversed in the following day. There appears more downside for Nvidia to respond to China's slowdown.
